subject: DPA: questions on offsite/escrow backups, deletion windows, and restore SLAs
messages:
From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medtech-solutions.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@medtech-solutions.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Questions on DPA - offsite backups / deletion windows

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and security teams have a short set of follow-ups for the DPA and SOC2 evidence before we proceed to procurement. Can you confirm the following for Redwood in-scope to the DPA?

1) System/service logs: retention windows (hot vs aggregated archives) and whether logs are included in customer-directed deletions.
2) Backups / snapshots: where are offsite backups stored, who holds the encryption keys, and typical snapshot chain retention (how long until final overwrite/purge)?
3) Prompt & payload retention: do customer prompts show up in backups/archives, and what is the timeline to purge prompts on termination or on-request erasure?
4) Restore SLA & proof of deletion: if we request deletion at contract end, when can we expect final irreversible deletion and can Redwood provide a deletion certificate?

We also want to understand escrow arrangements (if Redwood offers a backup escrow for cold archives) — specifically whether escrowed copies are retained by a third party and what the deletion/escrow-release process looks like.

If you can point us to a simple matrix that lists the artifact, default retention, end-of-contract deletion window, and any evidence we receive, that would be ideal.

Appreciate a short reply or a one-page summary we can include with our legal team.

Best,
Karen
Karen Liu
Sr. Contracts Manager | MedTech Solutions
[Attachment: medtech_dpa_questions.xlsx]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medtech-solutions.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA - offsite backups / deletion windows

Hi Karen — thanks for the clear list. I summarized Redwood's standard positions below and attached a simple retention matrix and our latest SOC 2 statement for your legal team. Happy to iterate on language for the DPA.

Summary (short):
- System/service logs:
  - Hot logs (operational telemetry and request traces): default retention 90 days. Hot logs are eligible for customer-directed deletion; we can expedite within 7 business days for scoped log sets.
  - Aggregated/analytics logs: retained up to 12 months for service monitoring and trend analysis; aggregated logs do not contain PII by default.

- Backups / snapshots:
  - Backups are encrypted snapshots stored in the primary cloud region and replicated to a secondary region for disaster recovery. Default snapshot retention (daily snapshots) is 180 days in hot backup tier; cold archival snapshots are retained an additional 540 days (total 720 days) before automated purge.
  - Encryption keys: by default keys are Redwood-managed. We offer customer-managed keys (CMK) for Dedicated/Private customers — with CMK, snapshots stored in backup are encrypted with your key and we cannot decrypt without your re-enablement.
  - Final purge: because of snapshot chaining and replication, final irreversible purge typically completes within 90–120 calendar days after a deletion request or contract termination (shorter timelines possible with a negotiated SOW).

- Prompt & payload retention:
  - Prompt/response artifacts used for inference are held in a short-term cache for 7 days by default for debugging/traceability. 
  - By default, prompts are not kept in long-term backups; customers may enable debug logging which extends retention to 30 days. We can commit to removing prompt content on customer deletion request from hot stores within 7 business days; removal from backups follows the backup purge schedule above.

- Restore SLA & proof of deletion:
  - Restore SLA: standard restore RTO for snapshots is 24–48 hours for hot backups; cold archive restores are 5–7 business days.
  - Proof of deletion: we provide a deletion certificate (signed statement + internal audit ID) when final purge completes. Preliminary deletion confirmations (hot-store removal) are provided within 10 business days.

- Escrow / third-party cold archives:
  - Redwood supports an optional backup-escrow program where encrypted cold archives are exported to an escrow provider. Escrow copies are encrypted with a customer-managed key (CMK) when requested. Escrow release or destruction requires a written request from an authorized customer contact and typically completes within 30–90 days depending on the provider and jurisdiction.

Attachments: retention matrix (redwood_data_retention_matrix_v3.pdf) and SOC2 statement (SOC2-Audit-Statement-2026.pdf).

If you want, Vivek and Lauren are copied in to handle any legal/compliance specifics — Vivek for contract wording and Lauren for evidence and audit processes.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_data_retention_matrix_v3.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: SOC2-Audit-Statement-2026.pdf (PDF)]

From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medtech-solutions.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@medtech-solutions.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:28:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA - offsite backups / deletion windows

Hi Mina — this is helpful, thank you. A couple quick clarifications from our security team:

- For the CMK scenario, can you confirm whether Redwood will still retain a copy of the backup metadata (not the key) and whether that metadata could be used to reconstruct data in any way?
- For escrowed copies: who signs the destruction order — Redwood or the escrow vendor? We need to understand chain of custody for regulatory audit.
- The 90–120 day final purge: is the upper bound driven by cloud provider snapshot chaining, or are there other retention/legal holds that could extend it further?

Also please send a suggested DPA clause for a 90-day final purge (we prefer the lower bound but need the contract language). If we can get a draft clause and a DocuSign-ready SOW for the CMK + escrow option, we can fast-track procurement.

Thanks,
Karen

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medtech-solutions.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 16:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA - offsite backups / deletion windows

Hi Karen — answers inline and I attached a short DPA clause draft and an SOW outline for CMK + escrow to the shared drive link. Vivek can iterate on the exact legal phrasing, but the operational points below should address your team's concerns.

- Metadata with CMK: Redwood retains backup metadata (snapshot identifiers, timestamps, size, region) necessary for restores and billing. Metadata alone cannot be used to reconstruct encrypted data; actual data blocks remain encrypted under the CMK. We can include a representation of allowed metadata fields in the DPA.

- Escrow destruction authority: destruction or release of escrowed archives requires written authorization from an authorized customer signatory. The escrow vendor performs the destruction and provides a destruction report; Redwood will co-sign the destruction confirmation when Redwood initiated the escrow. If destruction is customer-initiated, the vendor provides the certificate directly to the customer and cc's Redwood for records.

- 90–120 day bound: the window is primarily driven by cloud snapshot chains and cross-region replication. It can be shortened to a guaranteed 90 calendar days in the DPA for an additional operational fee and with CMK enabled. Legal holds (regulatory subpoenas, ongoing investigations) can supersede the timed deletion — in such cases Redwood will notify the customer and provide any lawful process required.

Attached links: https://redwood-share.example.com/drive/MT-2026-0987/retention-matrix (retention matrix) and a one-paragraph DPA clause: "Upon Customer's written request or contract termination, Redwood will commence deletion of Customer Data from active stores within 7 business days and will complete irreversible deletion from backups and replicated archives within ninety (90) calendar days, provided no legal hold exists. Redwood will deliver a deletion certificate within fifteen (15) business days after irreversible deletion completes."

Next steps:
- Vivek: can you review the DPA clause and SOW draft for CMK + escrow (link above) and suggest any legal edits?
- Karen/MedTech: if 90 days with CMK/escrow is acceptable, I can have a DocuSign-ready SOW and CMK onboarding checklist in 2 business days.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
